questions.question: The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) is a welfare programme being administered by which Ministry of Government of India?

options.text: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Rural Development**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP)** is administered by the **Ministry of Rural Development** of the Government of India.
 
• NSAP is a welfare program aimed at providing financial assistance to the elderly, widows, and persons with disabilities in the form of social pensions.
 
• It was launched on **15th August 1995** as a component of the Ministry's efforts to support vulnerable sections of society.
 
• The program includes various schemes such as the **Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS)**, the **Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS)**, and the **Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS)**.
 
• The funding for these schemes is shared between the central and state governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Ministry of Rural Development is responsible for the implementation of various rural development and poverty alleviation programs in India.
 
• Other major schemes under the Ministry include the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**, **Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G)**, and the **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihood Mission (DAY-NRLM)**.
 
• The Ministry aims to enhance the quality of life in rural areas by ensuring sustainable and inclusive growth.

questions.question: What is the main source of income for commercial banks?

options.text: Interest earned on loans and advances

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Interest earned on loans and advances**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Interest earned on loans and advances** is the primary source of income for commercial banks.
 
• Commercial banks provide various types of loans and advances to individuals, businesses, and other entities, and they charge interest on these loans.
 
• The interest rate applied to loans is typically higher than the interest rate paid on deposits, allowing banks to earn a profit.
 
• This interest income is crucial for the banks' operations, enabling them to cover costs, pay dividends to shareholders, and expand their services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Commercial banks also earn income from fees and charges for various services, such as account maintenance, transaction fees, and financial advisory services.
 
• They may invest in government securities and other financial instruments to diversify their income sources.
 
• Effective management of interest rates and risk is essential for maintaining profitability and financial stability in commercial banking.
 
• Regulatory bodies, such as central banks, oversee commercial banks to ensure they operate within the legal framework and maintain financial health.

questions.question: Which country’s Constitution was the inspiration behind the Directive Principles of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: The Constitution of the United States
The Constitution of the United Kingdom

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Constitution of Ireland**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution were inspired by the **Constitution of Ireland**.
 
• The concept was borrowed from the Irish Constitution, which aimed to guide the government in making policies and laws aimed at social welfare and economic democracy.
 
• The Directive Principles are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• These principles are not justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country, intended to be applied in making laws.
 
• The objective is to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• The principles emphasize that the state should strive to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting a social order in which justice, social, economic, and political, shall inform all the institutions of national life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written constitution** of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Directive Principles** aim to establish social and economic democracy in the country.
 
• They act as a yardstick in the hands of the citizens to measure the performance of the government.
 
• The principles also aim to reduce the inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities.

questions.question: Indian Industrialists reacted against colonial policies that restricted business activities and formed an organisation in 1927. What was it called?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Federation of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industries (FICCI)**__

__
 
• The Federation of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industries (FICCI) was formed in 1927.
 
• Indian industrialists formed FICCI in response to colonial policies that restricted business activities in India.
 
• FICCI played a significant role in lobbying for economic reforms and the interests of Indian businesses during the colonial period.
 
• It remains one of the largest and oldest business organizations in India, representing various sectors of Indian industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• FICCI has been instrumental in shaping the economic and industrial policies of India post-independence.
 
• It continues to work towards fostering economic growth and enhancing the global competitiveness of Indian industries.
 
• FICCI organizes various events, conferences, and forums to facilitate dialogue between the government and industry stakeholders.
 
• It also provides a platform for businesses to collaborate and share best practices.

questions.question: Who founded the All-India Forward Bloc Party?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subhas Chandra Bose**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose** founded the All-India Forward Bloc Party.
 
• The All-India Forward Bloc was formed on **3rd May 1939**, as a faction within the Indian National Congress.
 
• Bose aimed to consolidate the political left and to rally all radical elements within the Congress under one banner.
 
• He sought to establish a socialist state in India and believed in armed struggle against British colonial rule.
 
• The Forward Bloc played a significant role in the Indian independence movement, especially during the Quit India Movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose** was a prominent freedom fighter and a nationalist leader who advocated for complete independence from British rule.
 
• He was elected as the President of the Indian National Congress twice, in **1938** and **1939**.
 
• After differences with Mahatma Gandhi and other Congress leaders, Bose resigned from the Congress presidency and formed the Forward Bloc.
 
• He later went on to lead the Indian National Army (INA) to fight against the British during World War II.
 
• Bose's legacy continues to be remembered and honored in India for his uncompromising patriotism and his efforts towards India's independence.

questions.question: The Constitution allows __________ maximum members in Lok Sabha as of June 2023.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**550**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The maximum number of members allowed in the Lok Sabha is **550** as per the Constitution of India.
 
• The Lok Sabha, also known as the House of the People, is the lower house of India's bicameral Parliament, with members directly elected by the people of India.
 
• This number includes **530 members representing the states** and **20 members representing the Union territories**.
 
• The President of India can also nominate up to **2 members** from the Anglo-Indian community if he/she believes that the community is not adequately represented.
 
• The Lok Sabha is responsible for representing the will of the citizens, debating legislation, and ensuring the accountability of the executive branch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule **of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The composition and functioning of the Lok Sabha are governed by the provisions in the Constitution and the Lok Sabha Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business.

questions.question: Which of the following novels is based on the partition of India and was written by Khushwant Singh?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Train to Pakistan** is a novel written by Khushwant Singh.
 
• The novel is set during the partition of India in 1947, a period of intense communal violence and mass migrations.
 
• It presents a poignant and realistic portrayal of the impact of partition on a small village situated on the border of India and Pakistan.
 
• The story revolves around the lives of various characters in the village of Mano Majra, highlighting the human aspects of the tragedy.
 
• Khushwant Singh's narrative style in the novel combines historical facts with fictional storytelling to bring out the emotional and social ramifications of the partition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khushwant Singh** was a renowned Indian author, lawyer, diplomat, journalist, and politician.
 
• He is best known for his secularism, humor, and an abiding love of poetry.
 
• Some of his other notable works include **'The History of Sikhs'**, **'Delhi: A Novel'**, and **'The Company of Women'**.
 
• He received numerous awards and honors, including the Padma Vibhushan, the second-highest civilian award in India.
 
• Khushwant Singh's works often reflect his keen observations on society, politics, and history.

questions.question: Which institution mainly provides financial assistance and support to microfinance institutions in India?

options.text: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)** primarily provides financial assistance and support to microfinance institutions in India.
 
• SIDBI was established in **1990** under an Act of the Indian Parliament to aid the growth and development of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
 
• SIDBI offers **refinance facilities** to banks and financial institutions extending loans to the MSME sector, including microfinance institutions.
 
• It also provides **direct lending** to MSMEs and supports developmental initiatives aimed at strengthening the microfinance sector.
 
• SIDBI plays a crucial role in the implementation of various government schemes and programs to promote financial inclusion and entrepreneurship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microfinance Institutions (MFIs)** provide financial services to low-income individuals or those who do not have access to typical banking services.
 
• MFIs play a critical role in promoting financial inclusion by offering **microloans, savings, insurance, and other financial products** to the underserved population.
 
• The support from institutions like SIDBI helps MFIs in expanding their reach and enhancing their capability to serve the financially excluded segments of society.
 
• SIDBI also collaborates with various stakeholders, including the government, financial institutions, and international agencies, to create a conducive environment for the growth of microfinance in India.
 
• In addition to financial support, SIDBI also provides **capacity-building and technical assistance** to MFIs to improve their operational efficiency and sustainability.

questions.question: Mango showers are associated with which two states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala and Karnataka**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mango showers** are pre-monsoon rains that occur in the states of Kerala and Karnataka in India.
 
• These showers are crucial for the mango cultivation in these regions as they help in the ripening of the mangoes before the onset of the monsoon.
 
• They usually occur during the months of March and April.
 
• The term "mango showers" is derived from the fact that these rains are beneficial for the mango crops, ensuring a good harvest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pre-monsoon showers are also known by different names in different regions, such as "Kalbaisakhi" in West Bengal and "Nor'westers" in Assam.
 
• These showers are typically caused by the convectional activities in the atmosphere due to the intense heat during the summer months.
 
• Besides mangoes, these rains are also beneficial for other crops and help in reducing the temperature slightly before the arrival of the monsoon.

questions.question: The Padma Shri awardee (2016) Gulabo Sapera is known as the Queen of __________ dance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalbeliya**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gulabo Sapera** is a renowned dancer who was awarded the Padma Shri in 2016.
 
• She is famously known as the Queen of **Kalbeliya** dance, which is a traditional folk dance of Rajasthan.
 
• The Kalbeliya dance is performed by the Kalbeliya community, known for their traditional occupation of snake charming.
 
• This dance form is characterized by intricate movements and vibrant costumes, often resembling the movements of a serpent.
 
• Kalbeliya dance has been recognized by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Kalbeliya community** is traditionally known for their expertise in handling snakes and their knowledge of herbal remedies for snake bites.
 
• Over time, as snake charming became less viable due to legal restrictions, the community shifted towards performing their traditional dance to sustain their livelihood.
 
• The dance is an integral part of the community's social and cultural fabric, often performed during festivals and celebrations.
 
• Gulabo Sapera has played a pivotal role in popularizing the Kalbeliya dance both in India and internationally.
 
• Her contribution to preserving and promoting this cultural heritage has been widely acknowledged.

questions.question: Who among the following is the author of the novel 'Untouchable'?

__
 
• **Mulk Raj Anand** is the author of the novel 'Untouchable'.
 
• He was an Indian writer in English, notable for his depiction of the lives of the poorer castes in traditional Indian society.
 
• 'Untouchable' was published in 1935 and is considered one of his most famous works.
 
• The novel deals with the social injustice and discrimination faced by the untouchables in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Lachhu Maharaj is a celebrated ________ dancer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lachhu Maharaj** is a celebrated **Kathak** dancer.
 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of **Indian classical dance**.
 
• This dance form traces its origins to the nomadic bards of ancient northern India, known as **Kathakars** or storytellers.
 
• Kathak is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures and facial expressions, which are used to tell a story.
 
• It has three main gharanas (schools) – **Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras**, each with its own unique style and emphasis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lachhu Maharaj** (1901–1978), also known as **Baij Nath Prasad**, was a noted Kathak dancer and choreographer from the **Banaras gharana**.
 
• He was honored with the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** for his contribution to Indian dance.
 
• Lachhu Maharaj was known for his expressive abhinaya (acting) and delicate footwork.
 
• He contributed significantly to the popularization and development of Kathak dance in India and abroad.
 
• His legacy continues to inspire new generations of Kathak dancers.

questions.question: What is the name of the geographic feature that serves as a boundary between India and Sri Lanka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Palk Strait**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Palk Strait** is the geographic feature that serves as a boundary between India and Sri Lanka.
 
• The Palk Strait is a narrow stretch of water separating the Tamil Nadu state of India from the Northern Province of Sri Lanka.
 
• It connects the Bay of Bengal in the northeast with the Gulf of Mannar in the southwest.
 
• The strait is named after Robert Palk, who was a governor of Madras (now Chennai) during the British colonial rule.
 
• The shallow waters and chain of low islands and reefs known as Adam's Bridge (or Rama's Bridge) lie on the southeastern side of the strait.
 
• The Palk Strait is significant for its strategic location and its role in marine biodiversity and fisheries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India and Sri Lanka** share a maritime boundary that runs through the Palk Strait.
 
• The strait is relatively shallow, with depths ranging from 9 to 13 meters, making it difficult for large ships to pass through.
 
• The region around the Palk Strait has been historically significant for trade and cultural exchanges between the two countries.
 
• Efforts have been made to improve navigation and trade through the strait, including proposals for the Sethusamudram Shipping Canal Project.
